page: Amazon Web Services c9gd.48xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance managed by the Nitro hypervisor and equipped with AWS Graviton processors. The machine supplies 192 dedicated physical cores operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. Because each physical core runs a single thread, virtual machines on this profile avoid the resource contention commonly associated with simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 384 GB, corresponding to a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation of 2 GB per core.

A major architectural feature of the c9gd.48xlarge is its bundled local storage array, comprising 11,400 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. This massive local storage pool provides high-throughput, low-latency disk I/O directly attached to the host. Complementing the internal storage array is a 100 Gbps baseline network interface, facilitating rapid inter-node communication and large-scale data ingest. GPU acceleration is not present in this configuration, focusing resources entirely on CPU execution, disk I/O, and network transfer.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances compute intensity with local storage capacity. In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, integrating substantial NVMe capacity and 192 dedicated cores into a single ARM-based instance reduces per-thread overhead compared to multi-node configurations, though users must account for the ephemeral nature of local instance stores. The combination of dense arm64 compute, fast NVMe volumes, and 100 Gbps bandwidth makes the instance well matched for parallelized batch processing, log analytics, distributed caching tiers, high-throughput database clusters, and large-scale software builds.
description: Amazon Web Services c9gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by AWS Graviton arm64 processors. It delivers 192 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz with one thread per core, paired with 384 GB of system memory, maintaining a 2 GB per core ratio. A key architectural characteristic is the inclusion of 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The presence of non-shared physical cores prevents resource contention typical of hyperthreaded systems, ensuring consistent processing throughput across all vCPUs. The balance of high core density, extensive low-latency local solid-state storage, and elevated networking throughput makes this instance cost-effective for scaled execution without incurring separate networked storage access latency. Amazon Web Services c9gd.48xlarge is suited for data-intensive processing, distributed key-value stores, relational databases requiring fast scratch storage, high-performance computing, and parallel compilation tasks.
